Author: Raj Beer Singh
Bench: Raj Beer Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 77
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 7197 of 2023
Applicant :- Ravindra

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Mayank Yadav,Vivek Kumar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant-accused, learned A.G.A for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in Case Crime No.397 of 2022,
under Sections 376-D, 506 I.P.C. Police Station Gunnour, District- Sambhal with the prayer to enlarge the applicant-accused on bail.

According to prosecution version, on 04.11.2022 at around 5.00 AM, while the prosecutrix has gone into the sugarcane field to attend the call of nature, applicant caught her and committed rape upon her and co-accused Rajkumar remained standing there having a tamancha in his hand.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant-accused that applicant-accused is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

In her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C,
Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17241575/
1 prosecutrix has stated that applicant has committed rape upon her while co-accused Rajkumar,
having a tamancha, was standing at boundary of the ranch but in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C, prosecutrix has stated that first applicant has committed rape upon her and thereafter,
co-accused Rajkumar committed rape upon her.
She has also introduced one Chandrakesh and stated that said Chandrakesh also committed rape upon her.
There are material contradictions in the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
It was stated that prosecutrix is a mature lady, aged 28 years.

It is further submitted that earlier the applicant has lodged a first information report on 19.10.2022, under section 452, 376, 506, 120B IPC against one Rohit and Mukesh and that said Rohit is nephew of the prosecutrix.
It was submitted that first information report of this case has been lodged as a counter blast of the said FIR, by making false and baseless allegations.

Further, in statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., prosecutrix has also made allegations of rape against co-accused Rajkumar, who has already been enlarged on bail by co-ordinate Bench of this Court, the copy of which, is available on record.

Lastly, it has been submitted that the applicant-accused is languishing in jail since 14.01.2023, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant-accused is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
Learned
A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail, however, it has not been disputed that similarly placed co-accused Rajkumar has already been granted bail.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant-accused Ravindra involved in aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
1. The applicant-accused shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2.The applicant-accused shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.

3. The applicant-accused shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The applicant-accused shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
5.

The applicant-accused shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17241575/
2
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant-accused in accordance with law.
